# @dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego Makes [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) work properly with an [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/docs/go/) subscription: the model list comes straight from the gateway, and every inference request carries the `x-opencode-session` header the gateway requires. [中文](README.md) ## Why it exists A stock DSH route to OpenCode Go already works (`llm-pi-ai` ships the provider). What this plugin adds is what that route does **not** do: | Capability | Stock DSH | This plugin | | --- | --- | --- | | **Live model catalog** | A build-time snapshot: the fixed table pi-ai ships with, so a new gateway model waits for a pi-ai release | Reads the gateway catalog live, with multi-level fallback and TTL caching | | **Quota windows** (5-hour / weekly / monthly) | None | ✅ | | **Estimated spend** | None | ✅ | | **Per-model switches** `modelVisibility` | None | ✅ | This plugin serves the `opencode-go` route with its own adapter and adds the usage and settings surfaces. > **On the session header**: Go requires a stable `x-opencode-session` on every request and answers `400 MissingSessionID` without it. That was one of this plugin's original reasons to exist, but pi-ai implemented the injection on 2026-09-09 (`561a2e06`) and `llm-pi-ai` carries it automatically, so a stock DSH route does not miss the header either. This plugin still keeps its own implementation — it falls back to a one-off UUID when a session id is missing — until that fallback lands upstream; the review is in [`docs/scope-review-2026-10.md`](docs/scope-review-2026-10.md). ## Install Prerequisites: a DSH `0.2.0` release (`0.2.0-rc.1` or later; see "Compatibility"); Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`; `dsh` and `pnpm` on PATH. > **One owner per route**: a profile can have exactly one adapter for `opencode-go`. Remove the previous plugin (`dsh plugin --profile

remove @dan-ai-studio/dsh-opencode-go`) or clear any `opencode-go` provider in `llm-pi-ai` first. Otherwise the plugin logs an explicit ownership diagnostic and does not register the route — everything else keeps working. > **Using the Desktop app?** It does not install through the CLI — install, upgrade, and remove plugins from its in-app Plugins page. See "Desktop (Electron app)" below. ### Option 1: npm (recommended) ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego@ ``` **After installing, confirm it actually loaded** — `--dump-config` cannot prove that: 1. The startup output should carry the plugin's own registration line, `dshopencodego: route "opencode-go" registered as OpenCode Go` (with `enabled: false` it is `dshopencodego: disabled by configuration; …`). No line means no load — when the compatibility gate refuses the plugin, the same output stream carries `Plugin … is incompatible with dsh …`. 2. A profile without HMR reports `restart-required` (`restartReason: no-hmr`) after the install: the plugin takes effect only after you **restart DSH**. 3. Where the logs are: a failed startup writes the full diagnostic to `$DSH_HOME/logs/startup--.log` and prints that path; a failed `dsh plugin` run prints `dsh: plugin command failed; diagnostics: ` (a file under the profile's `.plugin-manager/logs/operation-*/pnpm.log`). 4. Whether the session header really goes out: `node tools/verify/live-check.mjs --check-only` is a **zero-cost** local pre-flight that prints the `x-opencode-session` and `x-session-affinity` this run would carry; dropping `--check-only` and adding `--allow-live` sends **one** minimal request instead (it costs money; rules in `tools/verify/README.md`), after which the script asserts and prints `OK x-opencode-session: `. > `dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep dshopencodego` is **not** load evidence: a plugin row the gate denied still appears in the dump (`packages/boot/app-boot/README.md`). It only proves the row was written into the composition. ### Option 2: GitHub Release ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego/releases/download/v/dan-ai-studio-dshopencodego-.tgz ``` ### Option 3: build locally ```sh npm ci npm run build npm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./dan-ai-studio-dshopencodego-.tgz ``` > Install tarballs by **local path**. A remote tarball URL against a profile that already has a cache hits pnpm's `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` (see "Troubleshooting"). ### Upgrade and remove ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add # upgrade dsh plugin --profile web remove @dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego # remove ``` > pnpm silently reuses a **same-named local tarball** (`added 0`). Rename the file when reinstalling a fresh local build. ### Desktop (Electron app) The DSH Desktop app is an Electron shell around the complete dsh Web application, and this plugin fits it the same way: the host half is a standard bundle patch, and the client half declares the `web` platform — the Desktop renders exactly that Web client, so the settings section and the in-conversation usage button come from the same client packages. The Desktop keeps its **own profile** at `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`, independent of `profiles/web`: credentials, model visibility, and plugin settings must be configured again there. Installation **must** go through the in-app UI — do not use the `dsh plugin` commands above: 1. Open the Desktop app → **Settings → Plugins**; 2. Enter `@dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego` as the install spec (or pin a version, e.g. `@dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego@0.1.11`), and confirm; 3. **Restart the app** when prompted, then enter the API key on the settings page (reference name `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`). Why: Electron owns the Desktop profile, and **the CLI cannot boot or mutate it** (Desktop README: *The CLI cannot boot or mutate this profile.*). Plugin management runs through the app's authenticated HTTP APIs and Desktop's bundled pnpm, so no `pnpm` on `PATH` is required. Upgrades and removals happen on the Plugins page too. The version constraint matches the CLI: the DSH bundled with the Desktop app must stay inside the declared and verified band (`>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0`, see "Compatibility"). If the plugin ever breaks startup, the Desktop's native recovery dialog can **disable third-party plugins, back up `cordis.patch.yml`, and restart** in one action — it will not lock the app out. ## Configuration Configuration lives in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: dshopencodego name: '@dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego' config: enabled: true # false withdraws the route only apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY # default baseURL: https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1 # default (OpenCode Go endpoint) # http(s) only, and no query or fragment; writing ?x=1 is refused when the profile is saved # or https://opencode.ai/inference/v1 (Console main endpoint, pay-as-you-go/free models) refreshMinutes: 60 # live catalog TTL, 1 ~ 10080 (7 days); stale past 24 hours it refreshes in the background anyway streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000 # stream idle timeout: longest silence between events (ms) keepAliveTimeoutMs: 600000 # connection kept idle between requests (ms, 1 ~ 1800000) # the timer restarts on every answer, so a connection in # frequent use is never dropped; a long pause in a # conversation costs one handshake (about 200ms) imageBudgetPreset: dsh # image budget preset: dsh / dshopencodego / pi-ai (default dsh, the host's own values) modelVisibility: # per-model switches; unlisted models follow the default rule (see "The model list in the settings page") glm-5: true modelLimits: # per-model capacity overrides kimi-k3: contextWindow: 262144 maxTokens: 32768 # optional: this model's output cap some-legacy-model: null # a whole-entry null: both fields explicitly fall back to the catalog values modelProtocols: # last resort: per-model protocol override some-new-model: openai-responses # the only legal values are anthropic-messages / openai-completions / openai-responses pinnedAddresses: # fixed IP: host -> address (only the gateway host counts) opencode.ai: 104.18.32.47 # IPv4 or IPv6; an invalid or absent address uses the system DNS requestLogEnabled: false # request-log master switch, default off: on registers the sidebar entry and the conversation tab; off leaves no entry and reads byte-for-byte as without the log requestLogDebug: false # debug detail: pool events and the request user agent; session ids are always whole requestLogMaxEntries: 200 # most entries to keep, 50 to 500; oldest are dropped first retryPolicy: # optional: this route's retry policy, executed by dsh-llm-retry mode: normal # or always (retry every failure; maxRetries is ignored) maxRetries: 2 # default 5 retryableCodes: [RATE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT] # optional: retry only these codes (defaults RATE_LIMIT / SERVER / TIMEOUT / TRANSPORT / EMPTY_RESPONSE) backoff: initialDelayMs: 500 # default 500 maxDelayMs: 10000 # default 10000, ceiling 2147483647 jitterRatio: 0.1 # default 0.1, range 0 ~ 1 ``` **Validated on save**: those constraints are checked when the profile is **written**, not at the first request — `baseURL` must be http(s) with no query or fragment; `refreshMinutes` ranges from 1 to 10080; `keepAliveTimeoutMs` ranges from 1 to 1800000; `requestLogMaxEntries` ranges from 50 to 500; every `modelLimits` field may be `null`, meaning "select the catalog value explicitly" (`modelLimits.: null` sends both fields back); `modelProtocols` accepts only those three values, and a wrong one makes that model appear as *configuration missing* (switch off, not selectable) rather than falling back to a guess; `retryPolicy` is a union (`normal` reads `maxRetries`/`retryableCodes`/`backoff`, `always` reads only `backoff`) and unknown keys are rejected. The API key comes from the Harness credential store (reference name `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`), or from `export OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY=...`. **Stream timeout**: `streamIdleTimeoutMs` bounds the **longest silence between two stream events**, not the total request duration — a long-thinking model that keeps producing events is never cut off. Default 5 minutes; the ceiling is `2147483647` (about 24.8 days). Exceeding it raises `TIMEOUT`, which is retryable. **Connection kept**: `keepAliveTimeoutMs` decides **how long a connection to the gateway is held between two requests**. The timer **restarts on every answer**, so a connection in frequent use is never dropped; it bounds only the silence between two requests. Default 10 minutes. - The reason is practical: once a connection is dropped, the next request pays a TCP and a TLS handshake again — **about 200 milliseconds** from here to the gateway — and that cost lands on the **first token of the next turn**. A pause in a conversation (reading the answer, thinking, typing) usually runs 5 to 30 seconds, which is longer than the HTTP client's own 4-second default, so **almost every turn paid for a handshake it did not need**. - This only affects deployments that **pin an address** (`pinnedAddresses`): with no pin the request goes through the system's own fetch, and this plugin adds nothing to it. - The settings page shows and accepts the value in **seconds** (a number of milliseconds is not readable at a glance) and stores it in milliseconds. Range: 1 to 1800000 milliseconds. - Once a connection has been idle that long, the pool **reclaims it** on its own — no separate mechanism is needed. The actual release comes a couple of seconds later than the setting, which is the client's own small margin beyond the deadline the server states. When the plugin is unloaded, the pool is **closed with it**: the pool belongs to the plugin and should not be left behind on the machine. **Request log**: per-request records, off by default; turning them on registers the sidebar entry and the conversation tab, and turning them off removes those entries and returns the request path to exactly as without the log. The settings page's "Request log" group holds the master switch, the debug switch (pool events and the request user agent, default off), and the retention count (default 200). - **Two entries, one page**: - **A sidebar icon → a full page in the main column**: every request across sessions. The log is a process-wide thing, so the sidebar is where it belongs — a fixed, always-visible spot, and the same pattern the Harness's own plugin manager uses. - **A "Request log" View inside the conversation**: this session's requests, in place — answering "why was that turn slow" without leaving the chat. - It is a page, not a floating card: the head, the summary (requests / failures / mean latency / mean first token / mean tok/s / mean cache hit / connection reuse) and the filters stay put while the table scrolls. Each row carries time, model, session, input/output/cache, **cache hit**, **tok/s**, first token, latency and status; clicking one expands its HTTP detail (first a **request timeline** — preparation → waiting for first token → streaming, plus the end tick, with per-segment milliseconds in the legend; then method, protocol, URL, body size, **preparation**, redacted headers, request shape, result and usage, reasoning split, cache writes, per-request cost, content span). **Preparation** is the local time from request start to the HTTP send — large means the slowness is local (cold catalog / images / history conversion); small with a large first token means the gateway / model side is slow. A dedicated sortable `Prep` column sits next to first token. Filters: model, result, slow requests, session; groups: session, model, result; **click a column head to sort by it**, click again to flip. - **tok/s** is the output rate over the decode window (first token to the end), on the same scale as the Harness's own per-turn reading (reasoning tokens included). A request that produced no token has no rate — none is invented. **A burst delivery has no rate either**: when the gateway holds a whole turn and flushes it at the end (common with reasoning models: 8 seconds of thinking invisible on the wire, then a hundred tokens in a few milliseconds), a sub-100ms content span is delivery shape, not generation speed — it shows as — and stays out of the mean. - The session column names the **session title** (from the session catalog; falls back to the id, whose full spelling stays one hover away). The session filter matches titles and ids; session groups are headed the same way. **Clicking a title opens that session** (an archived one refuses, and says so). - **Cache hit** is the share of input tokens served from cache (cache reads over uncached input plus cache reads). No reported input means no share — none is invented either. - **The In column is uncached new input**: the gateway reports a prompt as "uncached plus cache hits" and the log records only the new part — a fully prefix-cached turn reads as a tiny input with a 100% hit, which is not a bug. Hover a column head for its definition. - **Content split**: below the body size the detail shows **Text X / Images Y** — images estimated as base64 per deduped attachment (each capped at the route's encoded target), text as the residual, so the two always sum to the total. Image-dominated turns read at a glance. - Session ids are **always stored whole**: an id is a conversation identity, not a credential, and a truncated one reads two conversations as one. - The log i …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… **: the declaration is `>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`. What was actually verified here, in order, is `0.2.0-rc.1` (the dev-dependency baseline: gate verdict + typecheck + full suite), `0.2.0-rc.2` (the same plus a `prepareCall` generation freeze), `0.2.1-alpha.3` (the first target release), `0.2.1-alpha.4` (T-24), `0.2.1-alpha.5` (T-26), and `0.2.1-rc.2` (T-31, where the runtime moved to cordis `4.0.5`; the upstream contract layer had zero source changes). Other versions inside the range were not verified one by one. - **The upper bound is a tracking line**: `<0.3.0-0` means that the moment DSH ships `0.3.0-0` (the first prerelease on the `0.3.0` line), this plugin must ship a new release in the same window or every user loses the plugin. `tests/peer-coverage.spec.ts` asserts both ends — the lower bound accepts the installed version, the upper bound rejects `0.3.0-0` — so a drift here fails locally instead of failing on a user's machine. After changing a range, `npm test` is the verification (local mock gateway, no network, no tokens) — ranges follow what the interfaces declare, and are never "measured" with live probes. - **Peer coverage is now guarded both ways**: `dsh-typert-registry`, `dsh-client-ui-conversation`, and `dsh-client-ui-renderer` were imported by the source but absent from `peerDependencies`, invisible to the gate; they are declared now, and `tests/peer-coverage.spec.ts` asserts both directions — anything the source imports must be declared, and anything declared but unreached must be removed (`dsh-settings` went that way: the settings form is actually provided by `dsh-client-ui-settings`). - **Exemptions are per profile**: only a profile that ran `dsh plugin allow-version` has one, and no record means the plugin must stay inside the declared range. `dsh plugin version-exemptions` lists a profile's exemptions. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Cause and fix | |---|---| | Log says `another adapter already owns it`; the plugin's models are missing | The `opencode-go` route is owned by the previous plugin or by an `llm-pi-ai` provider entry. Remove the owner or clear its config, then restart. | | Settings page shows "Not configured" while requests still work | Pre-v0.1.4 builds had this defect (credential results were not unwrapped from their envelope). Upgrade. | | Install fails with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS` | A fresh profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` carries placeholder `allowBuilds` text; set `@google/genai` and `protobufjs` to `false` (neither needs to run scripts) and reinstall. | | Remote tarball install fails with `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY` | pnpm wants an integrity entry for a cached profile. Download the tarball and install by **local path**. | | A reinstalled local tarball behaves like the old build | pnpm reuses a same-named local tarball. Rename the file and install again. | | "The settings write was rejected" | Usually a concurrent writer (another window or process) holding the same profile. The plugin retries once automatically; if it still fails the view has reloaded — click again. | | The usage button shows "unavailable" | An endpoint or credential change invalidated the previous reading. Fix the configuration and press Retry. It never shows `0` in place of a missing reading. | | npm publish fails with `ENEEDAUTH` | OIDC did not match: check the Trusted Publisher's **workflow filename** (must be exactly `publish-npm.yml`, case-sensitive) and the organization/repository fields; run on GitHub-hosted runners with `id-token: write`. A `repository.url` that does not match the GitHub repository is rejected as well. | | A flood of `Accessing non-existent property 'Allow' of module exports inside circular dependency` | Caused by `pi-ai`'s **named import** of `partial-json`: resolving a named export from CommonJS enumerates the module's exports, and that package's `index.js`/`options.js` require each other, so reading `Allow` before its module initialises prints once per read — **a plugin reload turns it into a flood** (a restart usually clears it). **Removed at the mechanism since v0.1.38**: `pi-ai` and `partial-json` are now **compiled into the bundle**, so Node's ESM→CJS interop is not involved and there is no enumeration of an uninitialised export to begin with. That is a fix, not a filter. | | The whole DSH process stalls during ultra-long tool calls (multi-MB arguments) | Observed on pi-ai `0.87.1`: per-delta re-parsing of the accumulated arguments (issue #9265 / PR #9461). This plugin does not port DSH's consumer-side patch (ADR-0005); the bundled dependency is now `1.5.0`, so a recurrence would be upstream behaviour and would be fixed by an upstream release. | ## Development ```sh npm ci npm run lint # oxlint: static checks (the release workflow runs this too, and fails on it) npm run typecheck # both halves: host and client npm run build # build first: emits lib/index.js and lib/client.js npm test # contract tests against a real local HTTP mock gateway npm run seed # refresh the bundled catalog seed before a release (see "Releasing") ``` **Order matters**: `npm run build` must come before `npm test` — `tests/pack-contents.spec.ts` walks every `exports` target, and whether `lib/` exists decides whether that check runs or is silently skipped (it does not fail, it just stops protecting you). `package.json` no longer carries `prepare`, so `npm ci` will not build for you; all three CI workflows run `npm run build` explicitly. The suite covers configuration validation, the protocol ladder, gateway and online metadata, the catalog projection, the adapter on the wire (all three protocols), Remote contracts and services, session-header invariants, usage windows and the meter, the client controller and usage pill, both halves' mounting and registration, the error mapping for stream idle timeouts and aborts, the exit-code contract of the verification scripts, and several **structural invariants** (inject declarations match the source's reads, peer coverage holds both ways, the READMEs match the manifest, and the READMEs' claims about the upstream match the upstream actually installed). That is **61 test files** — a number `tests/readme-consistency.spec.ts` checks against the `tests/` directory, so it cannot drift. ## Releasing (maintainers) 1. **Version**: align `package.json`'s `version` with the tag you are about to push (`v`); CI checks the asset name against the tag. 2. **Seed**: run `npm run seed` to refresh `src/catalog/seed.snapshot.json` (public endpoints, no key) and commit it, so fresh installs start with a usable catalog. 3. **GitHub Release**: commit and push `main`, then push the tag. `release.yml` runs the tests, `npm pack`s, and uploads the tarball as the release asset. 4. **npm (trusted publishing / OIDC, no token)**: `.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` is manual-only and authenticates through GitHub Actions' OIDC — this repository **has no `NPM_TOKEN` and needs none**. Run it with: ```sh gh workflow run publish-npm --repo dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego -f tag=v ``` It verifies tag-versus-version, refuses to overwrite a version that already exists on npm, and the publish carries an automatically generated **provenance** attestation. It relies on the package's **Trusted Publisher** connection on npm (fields are fixed once created; to change one, delete and recreate it): | Field | Value | |---|---| | Publisher | `GitHub Actions` | | Organization or user | `dan-ai-studio` | | Repository | `dshopencodego` | | Workflow filename | `publish-npm.yml` (exact, case-sensitive) | | Environment name | (empty) | | Allowed actions | `Allow npm publish` checked (unchecked means staged-only: a maintainer must approve each publish with 2FA) | Additionally: OIDC publishing needs **npm CLI ≥ 11.5.1 / Node ≥ 22.14** (the workflow uses Node 24), and `package.json`'s `repository.url` must match the GitHub repository. Once OIDC works, switch the package's Settings → **Publishing access** to "Require two-factor authentication and disallow tokens" and revoke any tokens you no longer need. ## License MIT

# @dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego 让 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 正常使用 [OpenCode Go](https://opencode.ai/docs/zh-cn/go/) 订阅：模型列表直接来自网关，且每个推理请求都携带网关要求的 `x-opencode-session`。 [English](README.en.md) ## 为什么需要它 原生 DSH 已经能连 OpenCode Go（`llm-pi-ai` 内置该 provider）。本插件补的是它**不提供**的那几件事： | 能力 | 原生 DSH | 本插件 | | --- | --- | --- | | **实时模型目录** | 构建期快照：pi-ai 打包时生成的固定表，网关新增模型要等 pi-ai 发版 | 实时读取网关目录，多级回退 + TTL 缓存 | | **额度窗口**（5 小时 / 本周 / 本月） | 无 | ✅ | | **花费估算** | 无 | ✅ | | **逐模型开关** `modelVisibility` | 无 | ✅ | 本插件为 `opencode-go` 路由提供自己的适配器，并提供用量与设置界面。 > **关于会话头**：Go 要求每个请求带稳定的 `x-opencode-session`，缺失即 `400 MissingSessionID`。这一项曾是本插件的原始存在理由，但 pi-ai 已于 2026-09-09（`561a2e06`）实现注入、`llm-pi-ai` 自动携带，因此**原生 DSH 现在也不会缺会话头**。本插件当前仍保留自己的实现（为缺失会话 id 的请求提供一次性 UUID 兜底），待该兜底进入上游后再收缩——评估过程见 [`docs/scope-review-2026-10.md`](docs/scope-review-2026-10.md)。 ## 安装 前提：DSH `0.2.0` 系列（`0.2.0-rc.1` 及之后，见「兼容性」）；Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`；`dsh` 与 `pnpm` 可用。 > **路由互斥**：同一个 profile 里 `opencode-go` 只能由一个适配器提供。装本插件前请先卸载旧插件（`dsh plugin --profile

remove @dan-ai-studio/dsh-opencode-go`），或清空 `llm-pi-ai` 配置里名为 `opencode-go` 的 provider。否则插件会记录一条明确的占用诊断，路由不会注册（其余功能照常）。 > **桌面端用户**：DSH 桌面端不走命令行安装，安装、升级与卸载都在应用内 Plugins 页完成，见文末「桌面端（Electron 应用）」。 ### 方式一：npm（推荐） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add @dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego@<版本> ``` **安装后确认真实加载**——`--dump-config` 证明不了这一点： 1. 启动输出里应出现插件自己的注册日志 `dshopencodego: route "opencode-go" registered as OpenCode Go`（`enabled: false` 时是 `dshopencodego: disabled by configuration; …`）。没有它就没加载——被版本门禁拒绝时，同一条输出流里会打印 `Plugin … is incompatible with dsh …`。 2. 没有 HMR 的 profile 安装后会回报 `restart-required`（`restartReason: no-hmr`）：**重启 DSH** 后插件才生效。 3. 日志位置：启动失败会把完整诊断写到 `$DSH_HOME/logs/startup-<时间戳>-.log` 并打印该路径；`dsh plugin` 失败会打印 `dsh: plugin command failed; diagnostics: <路径>`（profile 下的 `.plugin-manager/logs/operation-*/pnpm.log`）。 4. 会话头是否真的发出去了：`node tools/verify/live-check.mjs --check-only` 是**零成本**本地预检，会打印本次将会携带的 `x-opencode-session` 与 `x-session-affinity`；去掉 `--check-only`、加 `--allow-live` 才会真发**一次**最小请求（花钱，规则见 `tools/verify/README.md`），脚本随后断言并打印 `OK x-opencode-session: <会话 id>`。 > `dsh --profile web --dump-config | grep dshopencodego` **不构成加载证据**：被门禁拒绝的插件行同样会出现在 dump 里（`packages/boot/app-boot/README.md`）。它只能证明"这一行被写进了组合"。 ### 方式二：GitHub Release ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add https://github.com/dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego/releases/download/v<版本>/dan-ai-studio-dshopencodego-<版本>.tgz ``` ### 方式三：本地构建 ```sh npm ci npm run build npm pack dsh plugin --profile web add ./dan-ai-studio-dshopencodego-<版本>.tgz ``` > 用**本地路径**安装 tarball。把远程 tarball URL 装进一个已有缓存的 profile 会撞上 pnpm 的 `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_TARBALL_INTEGRITY`（见「故障排查」）。 ### 升级与卸载 ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add <新版本 tarball 或包名> # 升级 dsh plugin --profile web remove @dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego # 卸载 ``` > pnpm 对**同名本地 tarball** 会静默复用旧内容（`added 0`）。升级本地构建时请改文件名再装。 ### 桌面端（Electron 应用） DSH 桌面端是 Electron 壳 + 完整的 dsh Web 应用，本插件对它同样适用：host 半边是标准 bundle patch，client 半边声明的平台就是 `web`——桌面端渲染的正是这套 Web 客户端，设置页分区与会话内用量按钮来自同一批客户端包。桌面端使用**自己的 profile** `$DSH_HOME/profiles/desktop`，与 `profiles/web` 互不共享：凭证、模型可见性与插件设置都要在桌面端重新配一次。 安装**必须**走应用内界面，不要使用上面的 `dsh plugin` 命令： 1. 打开桌面端 → **设置 → Plugins（插件）** 页； 2. 安装规格填 `@dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego`（或指定版本，如 `@dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego@0.1.11`），确认安装； 3. 按提示**重启应用**，再到设置页填 API Key（引用名 `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`）。 原因：桌面端 profile 由 Electron 自己拥有，**CLI 不能启动也不能修改它**（桌面端 README 原文：*The CLI cannot boot or mutate this profile.*）。插件管理由应用内插件页经认证 HTTP API 完成，使用应用自带的 pnpm，不依赖 PATH 里的 `pnpm`；升级与卸载同样在 Plugins 页操作。 版本约束与 CLI 一致：桌面端内置的 DSH 要落在已声明并验证过的版本带内（`>=0.2.0-rc.1 <0.3.0`，见「兼容性」）。若插件导致启动失败，桌面端的原生恢复对话框可以一键**禁用第三方插件、备份 `cordis.patch.yml` 后重启**，不会把应用锁死。 ## 配置 配置写在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`： ```yaml - id: dshopencodego name: '@dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego' config: enabled: true # false 仅撤下路由，插件保持挂载 apiKeyEnv: OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY # 默认值 baseURL: https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1 # 默认值（OpenCode Go 端点） # 只能是不带 query / fragment 的 http(s) 地址；写 ?x=1 会在保存配置时被拒 # 也可指定为 https://opencode.ai/inference/v1（Console 主端点，含按量/免费模型） refreshMinutes: 60 # 目录缓存时长，1 ~ 10080（7 天）；超过 24 小时未刷新会被视为过期并在后台更新 streamIdleTimeoutMs: 300000 # 流空闲超时：两次流事件之间的最长静默（毫秒） keepAliveTimeoutMs: 600000 # 连接空闲保留：两次请求之间连接留多久（毫秒，1 ~ 1800000） # 每次收到回答后重新计时，所以常用时连接不会被断开； # 对话中每次停顿较久都要重新握手一次（约 200ms） imageBudgetPreset: dsh # 图片预算三选一：dsh / dshopencodego / pi-ai（默认 dsh，即宿主自带值） modelVisibility: # 逐模型开关；未写到的模型走默认规则（见「设置页里的模型列表」） glm-5: true modelLimits: # 逐模型容量覆盖 kimi-k3: contextWindow: 262144 maxTokens: 32768 # 可选：该模型的输出上限 some-legacy-model: null # 整条 null：该模型两个字段都显式回退到目录值 modelProtocols: # 最后兜底：逐模型协议覆盖 some-new-model: openai-responses # 合法值只有 anthropic-messages / openai-completions / openai-responses pinnedAddresses: # 固定 IP：域名 → 地址（只对网关域名生效） opencode.ai: 104.18.32.47 # 可写 IPv4 或 IPv6；不合法或未设置时走系统 DNS requestLogEnabled: false # 请求日志总开关，默认关闭：打开后注册侧边栏入口与会话标签页；关闭后无入口，请求路径与没有该日志逐字节一致 requestLogDebug: false # 排错详情：连接池事件与请求 UA；会话 id 始终完整记录 requestLogMaxEntries: 200 # 最多保留条数，50 ~ 500，超限丢弃最旧的 retryPolicy: # 可选：本路由的重试策略（由 dsh-llm-retry 执行） mode: normal # 也可用 always（对所有失败重试，maxRetries 被忽略） maxRetries: 2 # 默认 5 retryableCodes: [RATE_LIMIT, TIMEOUT] # 可选：只对这些错误码重试（默认 RATE_LIMIT / SERVER / TIMEOUT / TRANSPORT / EMPTY_RESPONSE） backoff: initialDelayMs: 500 # 默认 500 maxDelayMs: 10000 # 默认 10000，上限 2147483647 jitterRatio: 0.1 # 默认 0.1，取值 0 ~ 1 ``` **保存即校验**：上面这些约束在**写入 profile 时**就检查，不会拖到第一次请求——`baseURL` 必须是 http(s) 且不带 query/fragment；`refreshMinutes` 取值 1 ~ 10080；`keepAliveTimeoutMs` 取值 1 ~ 1800000；`requestLogMaxEntries` 取值 50 ~ 500；`modelLimits` 的每个字段都可以写 `null`，语义是"显式选回目录值"（`modelLimits.<模型>: null` 表示两个字段一起回退）；`modelProtocols` 只接受那三个合法值，写错会让该模型以"配置缺失"出现（开关关闭、不可选），而不是回退到猜测；`retryPolicy` 是联合类型（`normal` 读 `maxRetries`/`retryableCodes`/`backoff`，`always` 只读 `backoff`），未知字段会被拒绝。 API Key 通过 Harness 凭证库提供（引用名 `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY`），也可以直接 `export OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY=...`。 **流超时**：`streamIdleTimeoutMs` 约束的是**两次流事件之间的最长静默**，不是请求总时长——长思考模型只要持续产出事件就不会被误判。默认 5 分钟，上限为 `2147483647`（约 24.8 天）。超时抛出 `TIMEOUT`（可重试类）。 **连接保留**：`keepAliveTimeoutMs` 决定**与网关的连接在两次请求之间保留多久**。计时器**每次收到回答后重新开始**，所以常用时连接不会被断开，它约束的只是两次请求之间的静默。默认 10 分钟。 - 背后的原因很实际：连接一旦被断开，下一次请求要重新做一次 TCP 与 TLS 握手，**到网关这一侧约 200 毫秒**，而这笔开销正好落在**下一轮的第一个 token 上**。对话里的停顿（读答案、思考、再打字）通常在 5 ~ 30 秒，正好跨过 HTTP 客户端默认的 4 秒，于是**几乎每一轮都在白付一次握手**。 - 这条只影响**固定了地址**（`pinnedAddresses`）的部署：没有固定地址时走的是系统自己的 fetch，本插件不加任何东西。 - 设置页里以**秒**显示与填写（毫秒的数字人读不出量级），存储时换算成毫秒。取值 1 ~ 1800000 毫秒。 - 空闲满这个时间之后，连接由连接池**自己回收**，不需要额外的清理机制（实际释放时间比设置值多约 2 秒，那是客户端在服务端给的期限之外自留的一点缓冲）。插件被卸载时，连接池也会**一并关掉**——它是插件的，不该留在机器上。 **请求日志**：默认关闭的逐请求记录，打开它才注册侧边栏入口与会话标签页；关掉它入口一并消失，请求路径与没有该日志逐字节一致。设置页"请求日志"分组里有总开关、排错详情开关（连接池事件与请求 UA，默认关闭）、保留条数（默认 200）。 - **两个入口，同一个页面**： - **侧边栏图标 → 主区域整页**：跨会话看全部请求。日志是进程级的数据，放在侧边栏最合理——位置固定、常驻可见，和 DSH 自己的插件管理器同一个范式。 - **会话里的「请求日志」标签页**：就地看**本会话**的请求，回答"刚才那轮为什么慢"不用离开对话。 - 页面是一整页而不是浮层：标题、统计（请求数／失败数／平均耗时／平均首字／平均 tok/s／平均缓存命中／连接复用率）、筛选栏固定在上方，只有表格自己滚动。每行含时间、模型、会话、输入／输出／缓存、**缓存命中**、**tok/s**、首字、耗时与状态；点一行展开 HTTP 明细（第一行是**请求时间线**：准备 → 等待首字 → 输出三段加结束刻度，图例带每段毫秒数；方法、协议、地址、请求体大小、**准备耗时**、脱敏后的请求头、请求构成、结果与用量、推理拆分、缓存写入、单轮花费、内容跨度）。**准备耗时**是从请求开始到 HTTP 发出的本地耗时——它大是本地（目录冷启动／图片／历史转换）慢，它小但首字大是网关／模型侧慢；另有独立的 `准备` 列可点击排序。筛选有模型／结果／慢请求／会话，分组有会话／模型／结果；**点列头按该列排序**，再点一次反向。 - **tok/s** 是**首字到结束**这段解码窗口上的输出速率，口径与 Harness 自己的每轮读数一致（含推理 token）。没有 token 的请求没有速率——不编数。**突发推送同样没有速率**：网关把一整轮攒到最后一次性推过来时（推理模型常见：8 秒思考在 wire 上不可见，然后上百个 token 几毫秒内到达），内容跨度不足 100ms，算出来的"每秒几万 token"不是生成速度——显示为 —，也不计入平均。 - 会话列显示**会话标题**（标题来自会话目录；拿不到时回退显示 id，悬停可见完整 id）。会话筛选同时匹配标题与 id；按会话分组的组头同样显示标题。**点标题直接打开那个会话**（归档的打不开，会明说）。 - **缓存命中**是输入 token 里走缓存的占比（缓存读取／（未缓存输入＋缓存读取））。网关没报输入就没有占比——同样不编数。 - **输入列是未缓存的新增 token**：网关把整段 prompt 拆成"未缓存＋缓存命中"两部分上报，输入列只记新增的——同一会话前缀缓存全中时输入很小、缓存命中 100%，不是 bug。悬停列头有口径说明。 - **内容拆分**：明细里"请求体"下面跟一行"文本 X ／图片 Y"——图片是各去重后附件按 base64 估的占比（单张按路由的编码上限封顶），文本是总数减图片的剩余，两者恒等于请求体总数。图片 dominant 的请求一眼就能看出来。 - 会话 id **始终完整记录**（它是会话身份，不是凭据；截断后两个会话会读成一个）。 - 记录的是环形缓冲（超限丢最旧），进程重启即清；页面平时只在打开与手动刷新时读快照，有请求中时每秒自动刷新一次直到结束，没人打开的页面零流量。 - 凭据永远不进记录：记录器根本不接收请求头参数，只收白名单里的会话 id 与 UA；请求一开始就有一条"请求中"占位行（状态列读秒），结束时原位补全为完整记录。失败的请求同样记一条（含错误码）——包括目录解析失败（未知模型）与凭证缺失这类"第一个字节之前"的失败，行里没有用量只有原因；消费者提前终止的流记一条 `ABORTED`，不再无声丢失。 **图片**：三个字段各管一层，超限的图片会被明确拒绝，而不是静默降质或丢弃： | 预设 | 单张像素 | 单张字节（base64 tag。 2. **种子**：运行 `npm run seed` 刷新 `src/catalog/seed.snapshot.json`（公开接口，无需 key）并一并提交，让新装用户开箱即有目录可用。 3. **GitHub Release**：提交并推送 `main`，打 tag 推送。`release.yml` 会跑测试、`npm pack` 并把 tarball 作为 Release 资产上传。 4. **npm（Trusted Publishing / OIDC，无需令牌）**：`.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` 仅手动触发，认证走 GitHub Actions 的 OIDC——本仓库**没有也不需要** `NPM_TOKEN`。运行方式： ```sh gh workflow run publish-npm --repo dan-ai-studio/dshopencodego -f tag=v<版本> ``` 工作流会校验 tag 与版本一致、拒绝覆盖 npm 上已存在的版本，发布时**自动生成 provenance 声明**。它依赖 npm 包设置里的 **Trusted Publisher** 连接（字段一旦创建不可修改，要改只能删了重建）： | 字段 | 值 | |---|---| | Publisher | `GitHub Actions` | | Organization or user | `dan-ai-studio` | | Repository | `dshopencodego` | | Workflow filename | `publish-npm.yml`（完全一致、大小写敏感） | | Environment name | 留空 | | Allowed actions | 勾选 `Allow npm publish`（不勾则只允许 staged publishing：每次发布需人工 2FA 批准后才公开） | 另外：OIDC 发布要求 **npm CLI ≥ 11.5.1 / Node ≥ 22.14**（工作流用 Node 24 满足）；`package.json` 的 `repository.url` 必须与 GitHub 仓库匹配。启用 OIDC 后，建议到包设置
